channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Egyptian wheat imports to be firm as domestic output increases
item.description: As Egyptian wheat imports in 2026/27 are expected to remain relatively steady from the previous marketing year, the country’s wheat production is projected to bump up, the United States Department of Agriculture attaché in Cairo reported on March 12.

item.title: Strong 2025 could mean complications for Canadian grain sector in 2026 says analyst
item.description: Carryover supply of many crops in Canada could complicate the market in 2026

item.title: Canada’s annual inflation rate eases to 1.8 per cent in February ahead of expected energy shock
item.description: Canada’s annual inflation rate fell to 1.8 per cent in February, after prices in the same period a year ago had risen sharply when the government’s sales tax relief ended, Statistics Canada said on Monday.

item.title: U.S., China discuss farm goods, managed trade in ‘remarkably stable’ Paris talks, sources say
item.description: Top U.S. and Chinese economic officials held “remarkably stable” talks in Paris on Sunday that touched on potential areas of agreement in agriculture, critical minerals and managed trade for U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to consider in Beijing, two sources familiar with the talks said.

item.title: Split market seen for Prairie farmland
item.description: Realtors have noticed a change in the farmland market, where values in the best regions continue to rise but demand for mediocre land is softer

item.title: Has Richardson rejoined the canola council?
item.description: The Canola Council of Canada has appointed a Richardson International official to its board.

item.title: Pulse sales to Middle East markets are ‘frozen’
item.description: Pulse shipments to the Middle East are frozen. It is a market that purchased $769 million of Canadian pulses in 2025.

item.title: Taking a look at the spring forecast
item.description: As promised, we are going to take a look ahead at what the latest weather models are predicting for the next few months, starting with the Old Farmer’s Almanac.

item.title: Conservation easements with limits have appeal
item.description: Developing a conservation easement, particularly those that forever tie a piece of land to an ecological use, can be intimidating, said a researcher who has studied attitudes toward easements in Alberta and Saskatchewan.

item.title: Canadian trade tribunal to examine imports of frozen, canned vegetables
item.description: Canadian officials will look into whether global imports of frozen and canned vegetables are threatening Canadian growers and processors.
